title: Higher-order optimisation under curvature: horospherical versus geodesic convexity

certification.note: Conceptual proposal only. No Lean-certified functor, implication, or direct sampling theorem is claimed.

candidate_hyperedges.label: Affine lower support to Busemann lower support
candidate_hyperedges.mechanism: Euclidean affine minorants and Hadamard Busemann minorants play the same proof role as global lower supports carrying first-order information into estimate-sequence arguments.
candidate_hyperedges.hypothesis_map: The target side needs the paper's strong horospherical convexity and Hadamard/Busemann geometry; geodesic convexity alone is not enough for this support statement.
candidate_hyperedges.conclusion_map: Reuse the abstract proof role local high-quality step + global support aggregation + coupling invariant while changing the concrete support geometry.
candidate_hyperedges.failure_boundary: This is not an equivalence of convexity classes and does not assert that every geodesically convex function has a Busemann minorant of the required form.

candidate_hyperedges.label: Negative-curvature divergence bifurcates into blessing and curse
candidate_hyperedges.mechanism: The same hyperbolic divergence sharpens horoball localization under global horospherical support while also enabling exponential packing of candidate minimizers under geodesic convexity alone.
candidate_hyperedges.hypothesis_map: Blessing branch requires hyperbolic/negative-curvature localization plus strong h-convexity. Curse branch requires the deterministic higher-order oracle model, g-convex hard family, packing, and controlled local p-jet interpolation.
candidate_hyperedges.conclusion_map: Expose one shared geometric cause with two opposite complexity consequences instead of storing the upper and lower bounds as unrelated leaves.
candidate_hyperedges.failure_boundary: No claim is made that negative curvature universally helps or universally hurts; the direction depends on the global support information supplied by the function class.

lean_graph_spine: p-th covariant smoothness => Riemannian Taylor remainder
